- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.2) in recent days — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.16) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction after price spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse quickly — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile — reduce first 5 days by 1–2% if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive, model often delays correction — apply a 2–3 day buffer for sentiment shift to take effect.
